ImageDescription.value: The tomb of Justus Gaule (1849-1939), German physician and physiologist, his US-born wife Alice, née Leonard (1859-1935), who was a physician as well, of their daughter Alice (1890-1933), who was the first woman to obtain a PhD in chemistry from the ETH Zurich, of their son Karl (1888-1922), who was a civil engineer, and of their daughter Madeleine Biber-Gaule (1892-1964) at the Fluntern cemetery in Zurich.

ImageDescription.value: The grave of Arnold Corti (1873-1932), Swiss chemist and entomologist, his wife Helene, née Stamm (1878-1948), and some of their descendants, including the philosopher and publicist Walter Robert Corti (1910-1990), who was best known as the co-founder of the Pestalozzi Children's Village, and his brother Ulrich Arnold Corti (1904-1969), a chemist and ornithologist.
